A more local-style experience
Sep 2018 • Couples
Our first real taste of Vietnamese food took place in Hanoi's Old Quarter. We arrived in time for dinner so immediately did the first thing the nurse who sorted out our travel jabs told us not to do - eat at a local street food place. 

Crouched on plastic stools we had our first taste of Hanoi spring rolls (we then ordered a second portion). And because it would be silly to have merely spring rolls for dinner, we also ordered a bowl of chicken pho and a BBQ plate where you sizzle yourself meat and veggies on a hot plate.

I would say that as long as you see locals at street food places like Quan Ngon Pho Co, and as long as your food is piping hot, go for it. You'll miss out on a more local experience if you don't - and you'll be denied the pleasure of paying a few quid for a filling and decent meal. (Yes, if I'd checked the reviews on here before we sat down we would have walked on... I didn't check them and we had an enjoyable meal.)

Just don't go there
Sep 2018 • Couples
Let me start with several cocroaches walking around my feet. I've eaten in several places much more "rustic" in the streets of Hanoi and they weren't as dirty as this was. 

We asked for 2 BBQ and they gave us a super tiny amount of meat. When I complained, they told me this was their portion for 2 people, that Asian people eat less... But when the bill came was only 1 BBQ set on the printed ticket and there were a +100.000 VND handwritten.

The actual food was tasty, but both me and my partner had "stomach issues" after eating there, if you know what I mean. In the same street we had a Pho soup that was literally cooked on the street and had no problem with it!

Small but capable
Apr 2018 • Couples
Dropped in for lunch as we were staying at the MK Premier across the road. Small narrow restaurant, like many in Hanoi, and mainly focused on bbq and meals cooked at the table. We went to try the pigeon that was advertised at the entrance. We ended up with a pigeon, some sesame goat breast and bbq'd some veg at the table. All very tasty and good value. I'd probably preferred the feet removed from the pigeon and the head not included, but that's the way they do it. I had to put ice in the beer which is not usual in Hanoi, that's usually reserved for further south. All in all a good experience helped by the very enthusiastic wait staff.
